chapters.title: Reactive traps & manufactured threats
chapters.deck: How warnings and interventions can help produce the very behavior later cited as proof.

chapters.title: Judgment, bias & decision errors
chapters.deck: Ordinary mental shortcuts that deception can exploit, without implying that every biased judgment is malicious.

chapters.title: Memory, perception & witness reliability
chapters.deck: Why genuine witnesses can diverge and why collecting first accounts matters.

chapters.title: Narrative control & information distortion
chapters.deck: Claims can be altered by omissions, repetition, selective detail, and deceptive provenance.

chapters.title: Groups, reputations & social influence
chapters.deck: How collective beliefs and interpersonal networks alter responsibility, loyalty, and dissent.

chapters.title: Coercion, threats & compliance
chapters.deck: Pressure that substitutes fear, dependency, or consequences for freely informed consent.

chapters.title: Abusive relationships & interpersonal control
chapters.deck: Patterns that can occur in intimate, family, workplace, or mentorship relationships.

chapters.title: Identity, authority & impersonation
chapters.deck: How claims of role, credential, status, or personal identity alter trust.

chapters.title: Confidence games & fraudulent persuasion
chapters.deck: Trust is cultivated, borrowed, or simulated to shift risk from an offender onto a target.

chapters.title: Money, assets & economic leverage
chapters.deck: Mechanisms of profit extraction and methods of hiding who bears the loss.

chapters.title: Sexual exploitation, grooming & consent
chapters.deck: Non-operational vocabulary for recognizing exploitative patterns while avoiding stereotypes about survivors.

chapters.title: Criminal networks, roles & internal incentives
chapters.deck: The social architecture of enterprises that coordinate sustained unlawful conduct.

chapters.title: Corruption, office misuse & institutional capture
chapters.deck: Separate actual misconduct from the mere appearance of improper access or suspicious outcomes.

chapters.title: Stalking, harassment & intrusion
chapters.deck: Patterns of unwanted contact and boundary crossing, assessed through behavior rather than motive speculation.

chapters.title: Threat assessment, aggression & escalation
chapters.deck: Behavior-based concepts for assessing risk without treating any one sign as proof of violent intent.

chapters.title: Crime scene behavior & offender inference
chapters.deck: Useful investigative concepts with strict limits on inferring character or diagnosis from a scene.

chapters.title: Interviewing, questioning & confessions
chapters.deck: The psychology of information collection, procedural fairness, and unreliable admissions.

chapters.title: Evidence, timelines & provenance
chapters.deck: What documentary and digital records actually establish, and what they cannot prove without additional context.

chapters.title: Digital deception & social engineering
chapters.deck: Human-facing digital attacks, described at the recognition level rather than as procedures for committing them.

chapters.title: Cybercrime incentives & digital identity
chapters.deck: Motivations and social structures behind digital offending, not exploit instructions.

chapters.title: Strategic deception, influence & intelligence concepts
chapters.deck: Analytical vocabulary for understanding adversarial information, without assuming covert involvement in ordinary disputes.

chapters.title: Platforms, online mobs & information ecosystems
chapters.deck: Mechanisms through which networked attention amplifies, distorts, and sometimes monetizes hostility.

chapters.title: Belief systems, high-control groups & radicalization
chapters.deck: Distinguish lawful religion or eccentric belief from coercion, exploitation, and demonstrable harmful behavior.

chapters.title: Trauma, victim experience & recovery
chapters.deck: Human responses after coercion or violence should not be mistaken for indicators of guilt or dishonesty.

chapters.title: Research discipline, ethics & analytical safeguards
chapters.deck: Controls against turning an intriguing theory into an unsupported accusation.

entries.title: Induced-Threat Provocation via Causal Concealment
entries.public_definition: A warning conceals that the warned person's intervention is what could trigger the predicted reaction.

entries.title: False Choice Architecture
entries.public_definition: Available options are arranged to conceal a reasonable alternative or make every visible option costly.

entries.title: Confirmation Bias
entries.public_definition: Information supporting an existing belief receives more attention or weight than disconfirming evidence.

entries.title: Scarcity Effect
entries.public_definition: Limited availability increases perceived value or urgency, sometimes independent of merit.

entries.title: Misinformation Effect
entries.public_definition: Misleading post-event information alters later recollection of an event.

entries.title: Confidence Inflation
entries.public_definition: Feedback or repeated identification may increase certainty without increasing original accuracy.

entries.title: Gaslighting
entries.public_definition: Manipulation leads a person to doubt their perceptions, experiences, or understanding of events.

entries.title: Firehose of Falsehood
entries.public_definition: High-volume, repetitive, multi-channel falsehoods can distort what an audience accepts.

entries.title: Triangulation
entries.public_definition: A third party is drawn into an existing relationship or conflict to shift its dynamics.

entries.title: Ostracism
entries.public_definition: Exclusion from a group functions as social punishment or control.

entries.title: Coercive Control
entries.public_definition: A repeated pattern restricts another person's autonomy through intimidation, monitoring, isolation, or deprivation.

entries.title: Economic Coercion
entries.public_definition: Control over earnings, debt, employment, or necessities constrains another person's choices.

entries.title: Isolation Tactic
entries.public_definition: Relationships with friends, family, or advisers are restricted to reduce outside reality checks.

entries.title: Rationalization
entries.public_definition: Explanations make objectionable actions seem reasonable after the fact.

entries.title: Authority Spoofing
entries.public_definition: Someone presents a fabricated official capacity to obtain deference or compliance.

entries.title: Impostor Syndrome
entries.public_definition: A person's unwarranted doubts about their own legitimacy or competence; not evidence of actual fraud.

entries.title: Confidence Trick
entries.public_definition: A victim's trust is cultivated and then exploited for an unauthorized gain.

entries.title: Fake Scarcity Offer
entries.public_definition: An opportunity is represented as almost unavailable to discourage comparison or verification.

entries.title: Embezzlement
entries.public_definition: Entrusted money or property is wrongfully appropriated by someone with legitimate access.

entries.title: Invoice Redirection
entries.public_definition: Payment instructions are falsified to divert a legitimate transaction.

entries.title: Sexual Coercion
entries.public_definition: Pressure, threats, or misuse of power undermines freely given sexual consent.

entries.title: Sex Trafficking
entries.public_definition: People are recruited, transported, or controlled for commercial sexual exploitation under applicable law.

entries.title: Organized Crime Enterprise
entries.public_definition: A continuing association coordinates criminal activity for material benefit, influence, or control.

entries.title: Straw Person
entries.public_definition: A nominal holder or participant acts on behalf of an undisclosed interested party.

entries.title: Bribery
entries.public_definition: A benefit is offered, requested, or received to improperly influence official or entrusted action.

entries.title: Process as Punishment
entries.public_definition: The burden of a procedure itself becomes a sanction regardless of its eventual outcome.

entries.title: Stalking
entries.public_definition: A repeated course of unwanted conduct creates fear or substantial distress under applicable definitions.

entries.title: Property Interference
entries.public_definition: Tampering with or obstructing personal property becomes a means of intimidation or control.

entries.title: Threat Assessment
entries.public_definition: Structured information gathering evaluates the possibility of harm and suitable protective responses.

entries.title: Protective Factor
entries.public_definition: A condition that can lessen risk or buffer against adverse outcomes.

entries.title: Modus Operandi
entries.public_definition: The methods used to carry out an offense, which may adapt as circumstances change.

entries.title: Organized Scene Label
entries.public_definition: An older profiling shorthand that can exaggerate the diagnostic meaning of planning or order.

entries.title: Cognitive Interview
entries.public_definition: A structured witness-interview method uses memory-supporting prompts to improve retrieval without supplying answers.

entries.title: Interrogative Suggestibility
entries.public_definition: A person is susceptible to adopting misleading suggestions during questioning.

entries.title: Chain of Custody
entries.public_definition: A documented history of evidence collection, control, transfer, storage, and handling supports integrity assessment.

entries.title: Evidence Contamination
entries.public_definition: Material is altered or mixed through collection, handling, or exposure to unrelated information.

entries.title: Social Engineering
entries.public_definition: Human trust, attention, or organizational routines are exploited to obtain access or information.

entries.title: Quishing
entries.public_definition: A malicious or misleading QR-code interaction directs a person toward phishing or another unsafe action.

entries.title: Account Takeover
entries.public_definition: An unauthorized actor gains control of an existing digital account.

entries.title: Data Broker Exposure
entries.public_definition: Commercial collection and resale of personal information create opportunities for unauthorized use.

entries.title: Reflexive Control
entries.public_definition: Selected information is supplied to influence the decisions an opponent chooses as their own.

entries.title: Disinformation
entries.public_definition: False or misleading information is deliberately disseminated with intent to deceive.

entries.title: Astroturfing
entries.public_definition: Coordinated messaging is disguised as spontaneous grassroots support.

entries.title: Filter Bubble
entries.public_definition: Personalized information selection can narrow what viewpoints a user encounters.

entries.title: High-Control Group
entries.public_definition: A group restricts members' choices, contacts, information, or exit through sustained social pressure.

entries.title: Identity Fusion
entries.public_definition: A person's personal identity becomes strongly integrated with a group identity.

entries.title: Acute Stress Response
entries.public_definition: Immediate physiological and cognitive reactions follow a threatening or overwhelming event.

entries.title: Secondary Victimization
entries.public_definition: Institutional or social responses cause additional harm after the original incident.

entries.title: Falsifiability
entries.public_definition: A proposition must allow observations that could demonstrate it is wrong.

entries.title: Ecological Fallacy
entries.public_definition: Group-level statistics are improperly applied to the behavior of a particular individual.
